All of my life in music and whatever happened to me right today comes from observing some of the musicians that were playing something. And I was always lucky to play with good musicians. When I went into Chicago I was sitting with Joe, Johnny Dots, Baby Dots and all of them good. Leo on piano and Joe Arroyo and Lauren at Horn. I said, why didn't we do it? Now, I went into the front set with Carol Dickerson's orchestra which was owned by Joe Glazer, my manager, and Joe Glazer and Joe Rollins who was called the…
I wouldn't listen to it. I've noticed you've talked a lot about Joe Oliver, and he must have been a tremendous influence.

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1961-02-10
items.q: Anywhere Joe Glazer sent me. I'll go.

ctx.x: You've been over there in Russia? I've been to Russia, yeah. I was slated to go to Russia with Ed Sullivan the week we played in Spileto. But I ate too much spaghetti one night and I'd stay there a week. You're going to go to Russia? I'll go anywhere. Just do it. Anywhere Joe Glazer sent me. I'll go. I mean, I just want to go to Holland.

Louie, do you feel that one of the reasons you're doing this is that America has been very good to you and you want to return? That's right. Back to return is when I just finished paying for my house. You better go back here. Yeah, I don't know another place. This is kind of a personal question, but what do you think are some of the faults that you have?

items.title: Louis Armstrong: Jazz Casual Interview, 1964-07-10
items.q: And then I went into the Sunset with Joe Glazer in 1926.

ctx.x: But that was really the first thing that I lost the memory.

Well, that was my life. That's all I knew of. Sure. But you have to get with different. Now like when I went with Fletcher Anderson's band in 1924. Well, there was something else. There was Don Richmond. The minute I get up on the stand to join the band, there's a part in front of me. You know, well, I was at least tall. And you get conscious. You know, your mind, as you go along, you've got to get with it. Yeah. So you lose something. But is that all good experience for you as a musician? I enjoy the experience.…

So all this added to your own equipment as a truck. As a truck. Yeah. And I didn't try to do nothing else but blows. And you would advise any youngster today to, I would assume, to have as much experience as a concert?
